options.content:
### Two planes. Never add them together.

A Zenoh message crossing the mesh is counted **twice on this host at this
instant** — once as WireGuard UDP on the physical NIC, once as TCP :7447
inside the tunnel. Same bytes, two layers.

| Plane | Answers | Denominator |
|---|---|---|
| **Transport** (below, first block) | *How much of my physical pipe is in use?* | declared link capacity |
| **Workload** (second block) | *Who and what is consuming the mesh?* | mesh transport total |

**Percentages are against a DECLARED capacity, not a measured one**, unless the
capacity source reads `measured`. A host nobody has characterised shows
`capacity not declared` and no percentage — that is deliberate, not a broken panel.

The **Unattributed** and **Off-mesh** rows are always drawn. A growing
Unattributed share means the category map has fallen behind reality, not that
the traffic went away. Full design: `docs/design/mesh-bandwidth-attribution.md`
(ADR 1128).

panels.title: Transport plane — how full is the physical pipe
Uplink used
panels.description: Physical NIC tx against DECLARED uplink capacity. Blank when no capacity is declared — never a guessed percentage.

links.title: What did this do to response times?

panels.title: Downlink used
panels.description: Physical NIC rx against DECLARED downlink capacity.

panels.title: Relayed share of mesh
panels.description: Relay bandwidth is metered and billed, and the same payload is paid for twice (node->relay, relay->peer). A rise here is usually peers silently losing their P2P path.

panels.title: Attribution coverage
panels.description: Share of mesh transport landing in a NAMED workload category. Never 100%: socket byte counters are TCP-only and short-lived connections close between samples. Falling over time = the map is going stale.

panels.title: Hosts with no declared capacity
panels.description: Each of these renders no utilisation percentage anywhere. Set node_exporter_link_capacity in group_vars.

panels.title: Oldest capacity claim
panels.description: A capacity nobody has re-checked is a claim, not a fact — and every utilisation percentage rests on it.

panels.title: Uplink — transport plane vs declared capacity
panels.description: Stacked classes sum to the physical NIC total by construction — off-mesh is the exact remainder. The dashed line is the DECLARED ceiling and is not part of the stack.

panels.title: Downlink — transport plane vs declared capacity
panels.description: Stacked classes sum to the physical NIC total by construction — off-mesh is the exact remainder. The dashed line is the DECLARED ceiling and is not part of the stack.

panels.title: Link utilisation over time
panels.description: Alert thresholds: warning at 75% for 15m, critical at 90% for 5m. Hosts with no declared capacity are absent here, not at zero.

panels.title: Top peers by physical-pipe bytes
panels.description: Transport plane, per mesh peer. The `class` column separates direct from relayed — a peer that is high AND relayed is costing the most.

panels.title: Workload plane — what the mesh is carrying
Bytes by workload category
panels.description: Socket categories EXCLUDING http-delegated, plus the HTTP plane — a clean partition, because Traefik's browser-facing sockets appear in both taps and adding them would double web traffic. Do NOT compare this total to the transport plane above; they measure the same bytes at different layers.

panels.title: Top workload categories now
panels.description: Bulk categories (image-pull, backup, audit-offload, replication) are schedulable around scarcity. surface-stream scales with concurrent viewers, not requests.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (category) (rate(goat_net_workload_bytes_total{host=~"$host",category!~"http-delegated|transport-underlay",direction=~"$direction"}[$__rate_interval])) * 8 or sum by (category) (rate(goat_http_bytes_total{host=~"$host",direction=~"$direction"}[$__rate_interval])) * 8)

panels.title: Web bytes by surface category
panels.description: From the Traefik access log. Static assets here are the cheapest thing to pin or edge-cache.

panels.title: Web bytes by service
panels.description: Which backend behind Traefik is producing the bytes.

panels.title: Headroom — what can I turn down, and what must I never touch

options.content:
When the pipe fills, the question is not *what is using it* — the block above
answers that. It is **what may give way so the critical thing keeps working.**

Shed order is declared in `ops/observability/bandwidth-categories.yaml`, one
home, and read from there by this dashboard. Highest first:

1. **`image-pull`** (deferrable) — Bursty hundreds of MB. THE canonical thing to batch off-peak: it is the usual cause of a link going unusable for minutes.
2. **`audit-offload`** (deferrable) — Scheduled bulk to cold storage. Retention is 30d; a few hours late costs nothing.
3. **`backup`** (deferrable) — pgBackRest. Schedulable; skipping a window is a judgement, delaying one is not.
4. **`filedrop`** (deferrable) — Operator-initiated bulk. Pause and resume; nothing is lost.
5. **`observability`** (sheddable) — Monitoring's own cost. Shed LAST among sheddables — shedding it blinds the decision.
6. **`messaging`** (sheddable) — Chat and push. Defer without data loss.
7. **`surface-static`** (sheddable) — Cacheable assets. Cheapest real win: pin or edge-cache instead of re-serving.
8. **`surface-stream`** (sheddable) — Live views. Cost scales with CONCURRENT VIEWERS, so capping viewers reclaims a lot for little loss.

**Never shed:** `identity`, `fabric`, `mesh-control`, `time`.
Mesh control and time are what you need in order to fix anything else, and
shedding observability blinds the decision — so it is last among the sheddables,
not first.

This is *declared policy paired with measured cost*. The panels beside it say
what each row is actually worth right now, so the trade is real rather than
theoretical.

panels.title: Reclaimable now — sheddable categories, worst first
panels.description: What you would actually get back by turning each one down. A category at the top of the shed list that is costing nothing is not worth shedding — order says what is ACCEPTABLE to lose, this says what it is WORTH.

panels.title: Protected — never shed these
panels.description: The floor. If these alone approach the declared capacity, shedding will not save you and the answer is more pipe or fewer peers.

panels.title: Reclaimable share of mesh
panels.description: How much of the workload is sheddable at all. LOW is the bad colour here: little to give up means no room to manoeuvre before the essential traffic is the thing competing.

panels.title: Protected floor
panels.description: Essential traffic. Any capacity plan has to clear this with margin.

panels.title: Headroom to declared capacity
panels.description: Spare downlink. Blank until a capacity is declared — the whole point of declaring one.

panels.title: Days to saturation at current trend
panels.description: Extends the capacity-forecast pattern to the network. Meaningless without a declared capacity, and honest about it — same predict-style projection the disk panels use, so read it as a direction, not a date.

panels.title: Peers driving $category (mesh sockets)
panels.description: In-tunnel socket bytes for the selected category, per peer mesh IP. Empty for the web categories — those peers are HTTP clients, in the panel beside this one.

panels.title: Clients driving $category (web)
panels.description: Per-client HTTP bytes for the selected category. Deliberately carries no `service` label — both would make the series count the product of clients AND services. Off by default above the goatnet scale envelope.

panels.title: $category over time
panels.description: Trend for the selected category only. Use it to tell a steady consumer (replication) from a bursty one (image-pull).

panels.title: Is this measurement trustworthy right now
Attribution sample age
panels.description: Older than ~2 minutes means the panels are showing last-known values that age silently. Treat as unknown, not as quiet.

panels.title: Sample gap
panels.description: The REAL interval the last delta covered — the denominator of every rate here. 0 means a first sample with no delta taken yet.

panels.title: Transport plane blind
panels.description: Hosts where `netbird status` was unreadable. Their mesh traffic reads as ZERO, which on a chart is indistinguishable from an idle mesh and is not the same thing.

panels.title: Peers sampled
panels.description: Connected peers in the last sample.

panels.title: Sockets sampled
panels.description: TCP sockets with readable byte counters. UDP has none — that traffic is reported as not-measured, never as zero.

panels.title: Web/socket cross-check
panels.description: Access-log bytes over the socket bytes for the same connections. Two independent taps on one flow: near 1.0 means they agree. Well under 1.0 is expected (headers and TLS overhead are on the socket and not in the log); near 0 means the access log has stopped.
